profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 56 Marietta Street, Atlanta, GA 30303, per mapping data. Digital Realty's own Atlanta listings show ATL13 at 1356 Marietta Street and ATL14 at 250 Williams Street NW, both different addresses; the house-number mismatch on Marietta Street was not resolved this session, so this entry is treated as unconfirmed rather than assumed to be ATL13.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Atlanta metro footprint, concentrated downtown near Georgia Power's service territory, with additional suburban sites in Austell also tracked in this registry. Atlanta has become one of the fastest-growing Southeastern US data center markets, with Georgia Power reporting rising large-load demand from data centers in its integrated resource planning filings. Digital Realty markets its Atlanta properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro within its global interconnection and colocation platform alongside its larger hub markets tracked elsewhere in this registry.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro market rather than per-building specifics for any US facility; this pattern of aggregate, not per-building, disclosure is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, and is not unique to this entry.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's Atlanta ATL13 facility occupies 84,000 square feet at 56 Marietta Street in downtown Atlanta. The operator publishes no IT megawatts, standby generator capacity, technical floor area, or power density for this building, only its total footprint and certifications. At typical colocation power density of 15 kW per 100 square feet, the building might support roughly 12.6 MW of IT load, but this is an assumption about density, not a published figure.

The facility holds SOC 2, SOC 3, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it to host security-sensitive and regulated workloads. Digital Realty operates as a landlord colocation provider, not a compute operator, meaning its tenants drive actual AI capacity deployment. The facility sits in Atlanta's downtown core near Georgia Power's service territory, part of Digital Realty's broader Atlanta metro footprint that includes additional sites in Austell along the I-20 corridor.

Georgia has published 66.3 MW of total data center capacity across 33 mapped facilities, of which only 4 operators publish capacity figures. This facility does not publish its own megawatts, so it cannot be ranked within the state's disclosed capacity. Atlanta metro has drawn attention in Georgia Power's integrated resource planning for transmission constraints on large new data center load, making the grid position of this market material to AI scaling feasibility in the Southeast, though this facility's specific power draw remains unpublished.
